{{Top|leg}}
{{Quote|Some believe the (sic) ''Darth'' itself is derived from the ancient Rakatan term ''darr tah'', meaning 'triumph over death,' or ''daritha'', meaning 'emperor.'|Darth Bane explaining the origins of the ''Darth'' title|<ref name="Book of Sith">''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]''</ref>}}
'''Darr tah''' was a combination of the [[Rakata (language)|Rakatan]] words ''darr'', meaning "triumph" or "conquest" and ''tah'', meaning "death." This led some [[Historian/Legends|historians]] to believe that it was a possible origin of the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] title ''[[Darth/Legends|Darth]]'' and that the ''Darth'' title could mean "triumph over death" or "conquest of death."<ref name="JvS">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref>
